name: starry-night
description: GitHub-grammar-compatible TextMate highlighter emitting hast; CSS-class themes matching github.com

host-language.comment: ESM-only JavaScript with JSDoc types (TypeScript type definitions are generated). Runs in Node.js (16+ for the 3.x line) and in browsers.

form-factor.comment: npm library only, with no CLI. The rehype integration is the separate rehype-starry-night plugin.

license.comment: Code is MIT. Bundled grammars keep their upstream licences, all described as permissive (MIT, ISC, Apache-2.0, BSD, MPL-2.0, WTFPL, Unlicense, etc.) and collected in the `notice` file.

documentation.comment: No dedicated docs site. The README holds the API reference, examples, CSS theme list and language list.

first-release.comment: 1.0.0 was published to npm on 2022-05-14. The repository was created on 2022-05-10.

engine-model.comment: Interprets TextMate grammars with Microsoft's vscode-textmate (a ^9.0.0 dependency). It is an open-source re-creation of GitHub's PrettyLights, not of GitHub's tree-sitter-based TreeLights.

regex-engine.comment: Uses vscode-oniguruma (onig.wasm, version 2). The WASM URL can be supplied via the `getOnigurumaUrlFetch` (browser) or `getOnigurumaUrlFs` (Node) options. There is no JS RegExp alternative.

embedded-languages.comment: The `text.html.basic` grammar includes `source.js` and `source.css` (both are in `common`), so HTML+JS+CSS works out of the box. Embedding works through TextMate includes and injections. Dependencies must be loaded; `missingScopes()` lists any that are absent.

language-auto-detection.comment: No content-based detection. `flagToScope` maps names, extensions and paths only.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: `flagToScope(flag)` accepts a language name, alias, extension or file path (e.g. `path/to/example.js` gives `source.js`). Grammars carry `names`, `extensions` and `extensionsWithDot`, mirroring GitHub Linguist. Shared extensions such as `.h` return only one scope.

resumable-line-state.comment: Internally tokenizes line by line with vscode-textmate's rule stack, but the stack is never exposed. `highlight(value, scope)` takes the whole string and returns only the tree.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No edit/reparse API. Each `highlight` call processes the full input.

semantic-distinctions.comment: A TextMate-grammar engine with no syntax tree or locals tracking. False per the guideline.

bundled-languages.comment: The README's language-level figure for `all` ("~600 languages", described elsewhere as "600+ grammars"). `lib/all.js` on main (3.11.0) imports 710 grammar scopes, some of which are helper or sub-scopes (e.g. regexp flavours) rather than distinct languages. `common` has about 35 languages. Checked 2026-11-18.

grammar-format.comment: Grammars ship as JS modules exporting TextMate grammar objects (`scopeName`, `patterns`, `repository`, `injections`) plus extra fields (`names`, `extensions`, `extensionsWithDot`, `dependencies`).

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Accepts any TextMate grammar that works with vscode-textmate once the `extensions`, `names` and `scopeName` fields are added. The bundled set mirrors the upstream grammars GitHub Linguist uses, and edits are supposed to go upstream.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: Custom grammars can be passed to `createStarryNight(grammars)` or added later with `starryNight.register(grammars)`, which is async.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: Each grammar is a separate module (`@wooorm/starry-night/<scope>`, typically 3–5 kB). Apps choose `common`, `all` or individual grammars and can `register` more later. Loading is user-driven (import, then register); there is no automatic on-demand fetch.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Uses the same upstream TextMate grammars as GitHub Linguist/PrettyLights (e.g. Microsoft TypeScript-TmLanguage, dustypomerleau/rust-syntax, MagicPython), so quality matches github.com's TextMate highlighting. Rated 4, not 5: some upstreams (e.g. MagicPython for Python) are older, and the set tracks Linguist rather than VS Code. Based on sourcing, not a systematic spot-check.

bundled-themes.comment: Nine distinct GitHub colour schemes: light, dark, dimmed-dark, colorblind-light/dark, high-contrast-light/dark and tritanopia-light/dark. They ship as 15 stylesheets: those 9, 5 combined auto-switching variants (both, colorblind, dimmed, high-contrast, tritanopia), and `core`, which has no colours. Version 3.11.0, checked 2026-11-18.

theme-format.comment: Themes are plain CSS files (each under 1 kB) that use CSS custom properties. VS Code or tmTheme files are not consumed; tokens map to GitHub's fixed `pl-*` class set.

token-classification.comment: Grammars produce TextMate scopes internally, but the output collapses them to GitHub PrettyLights' closed `pl-*` class set (e.g. `pl-en`, `pl-s`, `pl-c1`, `pl-k`) via a built-in GitHub theme mapping. Scopes are not exposed.

css-class-output.comment: Class-only output: spans carry a single `pl-*` class each, and there are no inline styles.

multi-theme-output.comment: One render serves light and dark. The unsuffixed stylesheets (e.g. `style/both`) switch with `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` using CSS variables, and the same class markup works with any of the shipped stylesheets.

public-token-api.comment: `starryNight.highlight(value, scope)` is documented and returns a hast `Root`, not an HTML string. There is no flat token-list API.

ir-kinds.comment: A hast root with up to three levels of `<span>` elements, each with one class, plus text nodes. Line endings are always direct root children, as documented in the README's "Syntax tree" section.

serializable-ir.comment: hast is plain JSON-compatible data with a documented spec, which qualifies per the guideline.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Output carries only `pl-*` class names, and colours live in CSS. Non-CSS renderers (e.g. ANSI) must map the classes to colours themselves.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: The generated hast nodes have no `position` fields. Offsets are computed internally but dropped.

custom-formatter-api.comment: There is no formatter plugin interface. The design is to emit hast and let any hast utility render it, and the README documents examples for HTML (hast-util-to-html), React (hast-util-to-jsx-runtime), rehype/unified and markdown-it. Contestable under a strict reading of the guideline.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: Nothing built in. The README only shows a hand-written example utility that wraps lines with `data-line-number`.

output-formats.comment: The package itself emits only hast. HTML with `pl-*` classes comes from serializing with hast-util-to-html (same author and unified ecosystem, documented in the README) or rehype-starry-night. React output via hast-util-to-jsx-runtime is shown as an example but is not counted as a first-party target. There is no ANSI or other format.

line-numbers.comment: Not built in. The README gives a sample hast transform for adding line numbers and notes that GitHub itself does not number lines.

streaming-output.comment: `highlight` takes a complete string and returns a full tree, with no incremental API.

terminal-ready.comment: The README mentions rendering to ANSI as a possible use of the AST, but no ANSI output ships.

native-dependencies.comment: Depends on vscode-oniguruma, which ships the Oniguruma regex engine as onig.wasm. No pure-JS fallback.

runs-in-browser.comment: The README has a client-side example using esm.sh and the `getOnigurumaUrlFetch` option. It warns that the WASM and grammar weight may be too heavy for browsers and suggests lowlight or refractor instead.

wasm-build.comment: starry-night itself is JavaScript and is not compiled to WASM. Only its regex dependency (Oniguruma) is WASM; see Native Dependencies.

synchronous-api.comment: `createStarryNight` and `register` are async because the WASM loads asynchronously. Afterwards `highlight`, `flagToScope`, `scopes` and `missingScopes` are synchronous.

bindings-ports.comment: No ports to other host languages. Related JS wrappers in the same ecosystem (rehype-starry-night, @microflash/rehype-starry-night) are not ports.

core-package-size.comment: The maintainer's figure: about 185 kB bundled, minified and gzipped for starry-night plus the Oniguruma WASM, before grammars. `common` adds about 250 kB and `all` about 1.6 MB. Bundlephobia measures the main entry of 3.11.0, which pulls in all grammars, at 1,915,514 bytes gzip, so it is not comparable. Checked 2026-11-18.

throughput-tier.comment: Pierre's Highlights browser benchmark (three.min.js ×10, Chromium 153, M4 Pro, recorded 2026-10-21): starry-night 3.11.0 (hast) took 10.5 s. Sugar High took 0.76 s, Prism 0.99 s, highlight.js 1.35 s and Shiki 4.4.3 28.3 s. That makes starry-night about 13.8× slower than the fastest candidate (Sugar High) and 10.6× slower than Prism, so >10× gives `slow`. The benchmark is a single run by the vendor of a competing library (Highlights), and its Shiki figure is notably worse than in other benchmarks.

initialization-cost.comment: Unmeasured. No cold-start benchmark covering starry-night was found. Async init loads Oniguruma WASM and compiles grammars, which suggests a cost similar to Shiki's Oniguruma setup, but there is no number to cite.

monthly-downloads.comment: npm downloads of @wooorm/starry-night for 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-18.

maintenance-status.comment: Regular minor releases (3.9.0 Jan 2026, 3.10.0 Jun 2026, 3.11.0 Aug 2026) that refresh grammars. Last push was 2026-08-30, within 6 months of checking, and the repo had only 4 open issues/PRs.

documentation-quality.comment: A thorough README with a full API reference, many examples (HTML, client-side, React, line numbers, unified, markdown-it), a theme table and a complete language list. There is no dedicated docs site and no migration guides, so 3 per the guideline.

notable-users.value: mdxjs.com (MDX docs site), unifiedjs.com (unified docs site), rehype-starry-night (official rehype plugin)
notable-users.comment: The MDX 3 announcement credits starry-night for the site's highlighting, and the mdx-js/mdx and unifiedjs.github.io manifests list @wooorm/starry-night and rehype-starry-night. GitHub itself does not use starry-night; it re-creates GitHub's closed-source PrettyLights.

bus-factor.comment: Titus Wormer (wooorm) made 169 of about 173 commits and is the sole npm maintainer. The other contributors have one commit each.
